source.text: Πάλιν οὖν αὐτοῖς ἐλάλησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων· Ἐγώ εἰμι τὸ φῶς τοῦ κόσμου· ὁ ἀκολουθῶν ἐμοὶ οὐ μὴ περιπατήσῃ ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ, ἀλλ’ ἕξει τὸ φῶς τῆς ζωῆς.

records.literal_gloss: Again therefore to them spoke the Jesus saying, "I am the light of the world; the [one] following me not not will walk in the darkness, but will have the light of the life."

en.L: So again Jesus spoke to them, saying, "I am the light of the world; the one who follows {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will certainly not walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life."
en.B: Jesus spoke to them once more: "I am the light of the world. Those who follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will never walk in the darkness; they will have the light of life."
en.R: Jesus spoke to the people again. He said, "I am the light of the world. People who follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will never walk in the dark. They will have the light that gives life."

es.L: Otra vez, pues, Jesús les habló, diciendo: «Yo soy la luz del mundo; el que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} sigue de ningún modo andará en la oscuridad, sino que tendrá la luz de la vida».
es.B: Jesús volvió a hablarles: «Yo soy la luz del mundo. Los que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} siguen nunca andarán en la oscuridad; tendrán la luz de la vida».
es.R: Jesús volvió a hablarle a la gente. Les dijo: «Yo soy la luz del mundo. Los que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} siguen nunca andarán en la oscuridad. Tendrán la luz que da vida».

fr.L: Jésus leur parla donc de nouveau, disant : « Je suis la lumière du monde ; celui qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} suit ne marchera certainement pas dans les ténèbres, mais aura la lumière de la vie. »
fr.B: Jésus leur adressa de nouveau la parole : « Je suis la lumière du monde. Ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} suivent ne marcheront jamais dans les ténèbres ; ils auront la lumière de la vie. »
fr.R: Jésus a de nouveau parlé aux gens. Il a dit : « Je suis la lumière du monde. Ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} suivent ne marcheront jamais dans le noir. Ils auront la lumière qui donne la vie. »

sw.L: Basi Yesu akasema nao tena, akisema, "Mimi ni nuru ya ulimwengu; anayenifuata hakika hatatembea gizani, bali nuru ya uzima itakuwa yake."
sw.B: Yesu akasema nao tena: "Mimi ni nuru ya ulimwengu. Wale wanaonifuata hawatatembea gizani kamwe; watakuwa na nuru ya uzima."
sw.R: Yesu akasema na watu tena. Akasema, "Mimi ni nuru ya ulimwengu. Watu wanaonifuata hawatatembea gizani kamwe. Watakuwa na nuru inayoleta uzima."

vi.L: Vậy Đức Giê-xu lại nói với họ rằng: "Ta là ánh sáng của thế gian; người nào theo {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chắc chắn sẽ không bước đi trong bóng tối, nhưng sẽ có ánh sáng của sự sống."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu lại nói với họ: "Ta là ánh sáng của thế gian. Ai theo {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không bao giờ bước đi trong bóng tối, nhưng sẽ có ánh sáng của sự sống."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu lại nói với dân chúng: "Ta là ánh sáng của thế gian. Ai theo {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không bao giờ đi trong bóng tối. Người ấy sẽ có ánh sáng ban sự sống."

ko.L: 그러자 예수께서 다시 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "나는 세상의 빛이다. 나를 따르는 사람은 결코 어둠 속에서 다니지 않고, 생명의 빛을 가질 것이다."
ko.B: 예수께서 다시 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "나는 세상의 빛이다. 나를 따르는 사람은 결코 어둠 속을 걷지 않고, 생명의 빛을 얻을 것이다."
ko.R: 예수께서 다시 사람들에게 말씀하셨다. "나는 세상의 빛이다. 나를 따르는 사람은 절대로 어둠 속에서 다니지 않을 것이다. 그 사람은 생명을 주는 빛을 받을 것이다."

decisions.choice: again, so: Jesus speaks once more to the crowd at the Festival of Tabernacles, taking up the scene of 7:37-52
alternatives: a new occasion, unconnected to the feast
decisions.reason: The words point back to Jesus's public teaching at the feast (7:14, 28, 37). The disputed story of 7:53-8:11 now stands between, but it was not part of the earliest copies of John (see the note at 7:53), and without it 8:12 follows straight on from 7:52: the Pharisees have just dismissed Jesus, and he speaks again in the temple (8:20). "Them" are the people gathered there, with Pharisees among them (8:13).

decisions.choice: I am the light of the world: the second of John's sayings "I am" with a picture; the world here is all humanity
decisions.reason: With a predicate, "I am" is ordinary grammar, as in 6:35; the "I" is written out and emphatic. The saying takes up the prologue, where the Word is the light of humanity, the true light coming into the world (1:4-9), and it returns at 9:5 before Jesus gives sight to a man born blind. The world here is humanity as a whole, all people living in the dark without God, not one nation only (compare 3:19; 12:46).

decisions.choice: light at the feast: the lamps of Tabernacles, the pillar of fire, and the light God promised in Isaiah
decisions.reason: The saying is spoken at the Festival of Tabernacles, in the temple near the treasury (8:20). Later Jewish tradition (Mishnah Sukkah 5:2-4) describes great lamps lit in the temple courts during the feast, so bright that they lit up Jerusalem; John does not mention them, so the link is likely but not certain. The feast recalled Israel's years in the wilderness (Leviticus 23:42-43), when God went before the people in a pillar of fire to give them light (Exodus 13:21), and Israel followed. Isaiah promises that the people who walk in darkness will see a great light (Isaiah 9:2) and that God's servant will be a light to the nations (Isaiah 42:6; 49:6).

decisions.choice: will certainly not walk in the darkness; the light of life: the light that gives life
decisions.reason: The double negative is the strongest way to say "not" in Greek. To walk is to live one's life, and the darkness is the world without God, as in 1:5 and 12:35, 46. In "the light of life" the genitive describes what the light gives: life, as the bread of life is the bread that gives life (6:35); the light also belongs to life itself, since the Word's life was the light (1:4).

decisions.choice: the people; the light that gives life
alternatives: them; the light of life (Literal, Balanced)
decisions.reason: Readable names who "them" are (meaning decision m1) and states the sense of "the light of life" (meaning decision m4). Literal and Balanced keep the familiar phrase, which is the plain translation.

decisions.choice: Those who follow (B), People who follow (R) ... never
decisions.reason: The Greek "the one following" means anyone at all; a plural keeps that sense without a he or she. "Never" carries the emphatic negative (meaning decision m4), as in 6:35.

decisions.choice: la oscuridad; los que me siguen (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Oscuridad" as at 1:5 and 3:19. Balanced and Readable use the plural, which is general, as English does; Literal keeps "el que". Every plural "you" in this passage is the ustedes / vosotros setting, and every pronoun Spanish writes for Christ or God takes the deity_pronoun setting, by the book-wide rule (decision r-es-3).

decisions.choice: la luz que da vida
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable states the sense of "la luz de la vida" (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for the passage (8:12-20), as in 1:19. The passé simple ("parla", "répondit") is the normal tense of written narrative; Readable uses the passé composé ("a parlé", "a répondu"), the past tense French readers speak and learn first. The imperfect ("disaient", 8:19) gives the Greek imperfect.

decisions.choice: les ténèbres (L, B); le noir (R)
decisions.reason: "Les ténèbres" is the word French uses for John's darkness throughout (1:5; 12:35, 46) and keeps the link with them. It is a literary word, so Readable says "dans le noir", as English Readable says "in the dark".

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the reader setting has nothing to change. Respect for Jesus is carried by the subject honorific ("-시-", "께서") and "그분" in the narrative at every level; Jesus speaks in the plain style (해라체) as everywhere in the book. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: el que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} sigue (L); los que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} siguen (B, R)
alternatives: stressed pronouns only (él, mí, ti, sí, tú)
decisions.reason: Book-wide rule for John in Spanish, as for Mark (Mark 1:2) and the other books: every pronoun Spanish writes for God or Christ takes the deity_pronoun setting, whether stressed (él, mí, ti, sí, tú), possessive (su, sus, mi, mis, tu, tus, mío, suyo) or an object pronoun standing before the verb (lo, le, me, te, and "se" where it stands for "le"). A pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plain, as English writes "He"; so is a pronoun joined to the end of a verb ("sígueme", "créanme"), "conmigo" and "contigo", and a reflexive ("me voy", "te haces"). Pronouns for the Spirit follow the same rule, as in English. Pronouns for anyone else, including the shepherd of the picture in 10:1-5, take no span.

source.text: εἶπον οὖν αὐτῷ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι· Σὺ περὶ σεαυτοῦ μαρτυρεῖς· ἡ μαρτυρία σου οὐκ ἔστιν ἀληθής.

records.literal_gloss: Said therefore to him the Pharisees, "You about yourself testify; the testimony of you not is true."

en.L: So the Pharisees said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "You are testifying about {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}; {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} testimony is not true."
en.B: The Pharisees then said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "You are testifying on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own behalf; {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} testimony is not true."
en.R: The Pharisees said to Jesus, "You are the only witness speaking about {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}. So {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} testimony does not count as true."

es.L: Le dijeron, pues, los fariseos: «Tú das testimonio acerca de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} mismo; {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} testimonio no es verdadero».
es.B: Entonces los fariseos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «Estás testificando a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} propio favor; {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} testimonio no es verdadero».
es.R: Los fariseos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron a Jesús: «Tú eres el único que habla a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} favor. Así que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} testimonio no se puede tomar como verdadero».

fr.L: Les Pharisiens {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dirent donc : « Tu rends témoignage de {{deity_pronoun:toi-même|Toi-même}} ; {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} témoignage n’est pas vrai. »
fr.B: Les Pharisiens {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dirent alors : « Tu rends témoignage en {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} propre faveur ; {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} témoignage n’est pas vrai. »
fr.R: Les Pharisiens ont dit à Jésus : « Tu es seul à témoigner en {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} faveur. Alors {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} témoignage ne peut pas être reconnu comme vrai. »

sw.L: Basi Mafarisayo wakamwambia, "Wewe unajishuhudia {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}; ushuhuda {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} si kweli."
sw.B: Mafarisayo wakamwambia, "Unatoa ushuhuda juu {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}; ushuhuda {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} si kweli."
sw.R: Mafarisayo wakamwambia Yesu, "Wewe ndiwe shahidi pekee unayeshuhudia habari {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}}. Kwa hiyo ushuhuda {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} hauhesabiwi kuwa kweli."

vi.L: Vậy người Pha-ri-si nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ông tự làm chứng về mình; lời chứng của ông không thật."
vi.B: Người Pha-ri-si bèn nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ông tự làm chứng cho chính mình; lời chứng của ông không thật."
vi.R: Người Pha-ri-si nói với Đức Giê-xu: "Chỉ có mình ông làm chứng về chính ông. Vậy lời chứng của ông không được coi là thật."

ko.L: 그러자 바리새파 사람들이 그분께 말했다. "네가 너 자신에 대하여 증언하고 있으니, 네 증언은 참되지 않다."
ko.B: 그러자 바리새파 사람들이 그분께 말했다. "너는 너 자신을 위해 증언하고 있다. 그러니 네 증언은 참되지 않다."
ko.R: 바리새파 사람들이 예수께 말했다. "너는 너 자신에 대해 혼자서 증언하고 있다. 그러니 네 증언은 참된 증언으로 인정할 수 없다."

decisions.choice: true: valid as evidence, able to stand in a court
alternatives: true as opposed to false: a charge that Jesus is lying
decisions.reason: The Pharisees speak in the terms of the law, which lets a matter stand only on the evidence of two or three witnesses (Deuteronomy 19:15). A claim about oneself, with no one else to support it, does not count as proof. They are not saying that Jesus lies but that his word alone proves nothing.

decisions.choice: the Pharisees use Jesus's own words against him
decisions.reason: In 5:31 Jesus himself granted the rule: "If I testify about myself, my testimony is not true." The Pharisees now apply it to his claim to be the light of the world (8:12). Jesus answers in 8:14-18, as he did in 5:32-37, by naming the Father as the second witness.

decisions.choice: You about yourself: the emphasis falls on Jesus as the one speaking about himself
decisions.reason: The pronoun "you" is written out and stands first, and "about yourself" comes before the verb. The stress is on who is giving the evidence.

decisions.choice: on your own behalf (B); the only witness ... does not count as true (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording as 5:31, where Jesus states the rule the Pharisees now quote, so that readers can hear the echo. Readable spells out the legal point (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: a tu propio favor (B); el único que habla a tu favor ... no se puede tomar como verdadero (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording as 5:31, where Jesus states the rule the Pharisees now quote, so readers can hear the echo (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}
decisions.reason: "Ti" in "acerca de ti mismo" is a stressed pronoun for Christ, so it takes the deity_pronoun setting, as do "le" and "tu" for him in Balanced and Readable, by the book-wide rule for Spanish (see 8:12).

decisions.choice: rendre témoignage (L, B); témoigner (R); n’est pas vrai (L, B); ne peut pas être reconnu comme vrai (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide words for testimony in John. "Vrai" here means valid as evidence (meaning decision m1); "valable" would say that and lose the word "vrai" Jesus takes up in verse 14, so Literal and Balanced keep "vrai" and Readable spells out the legal sense.

decisions.choice: The Pharisees speak to Jesus in the plain style ("너", "참되지 않다")
alternatives: formal polite style (합쇼체: "당신의 증언은 참되지 않습니다")
decisions.reason: The style guide allows open opponents to speak to Jesus without honorifics where the scene is hostile; here they reject his testimony to his face. This holds through the dispute in this passage.

decisions.choice: "ông" for Jesus in the Pharisees' mouth, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Opponents address Jesus as "ông", polite but without the respect of "Thầy", as the guide sets. It is a noun of address and takes no span, where the English has "you", "your" under the setting. This holds for the whole passage.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Κἂν ἐγὼ μαρτυρῶ περὶ ἐμαυτοῦ, ἀληθής ἐστιν ἡ μαρτυρία μου, ὅτι οἶδα πόθεν ἦλθον καὶ ποῦ ὑπάγω· ὑμεῖς δὲ οὐκ οἴδατε πόθεν ἔρχομαι ἢ ποῦ ὑπάγω.

records.literal_gloss: Answered Jesus and said to them, "Even if I testify about myself, true is the testimony of me, because I know from where I came and where I go; you but not know from where I come or where I go.

en.L: Jesus answered and said to them, "Even if I testify about {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} testimony is true, because I know where I came from and where I am going; but you do not know where I come from or where I am going.
en.B: Jesus replied, "Even if I do testify on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own behalf, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} testimony is true, since I know where I came from and where I am going. You, however, have no idea where I come from or where I am going.
en.R: Jesus answered, "Even if I am a witness speaking about {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} testimony is true. I know where I came from, and I know where I am going. But you do not know where I come from or where I am going.

es.L: Respondió Jesús y les dijo: «Aunque yo doy testimonio acerca de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} mismo, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} testimonio es verdadero, porque sé de dónde vine y adónde voy; pero {{plural_you:ustedes no saben|vosotros no sabéis}} de dónde vengo ni adónde voy.
es.B: Jesús les respondió: «Aunque testifique a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} propio favor, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} testimonio es verdadero, porque sé de dónde vine y adónde voy. {{plural_you:Ustedes, en cambio, no tienen|Vosotros, en cambio, no tenéis}} idea de dónde vengo ni adónde voy.
es.R: Jesús les respondió: «Aunque yo sea un testigo que habla de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} mismo, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} testimonio es verdadero. Sé de dónde vine, y sé adónde voy. Pero {{plural_you:ustedes no saben|vosotros no sabéis}} de dónde vengo ni adónde voy.

fr.L: Jésus répondit et leur dit : « Même si je rends témoignage de {{deity_pronoun:moi-même|Moi-même}}, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} témoignage est vrai, parce que je sais d’où je suis venu et où je vais ; mais vous, vous ne savez pas d’où je viens ni où je vais.
fr.B: Jésus répondit : « Même si je rends témoignage en {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} propre faveur, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} témoignage est vrai, car je sais d’où je suis venu et où je vais. Vous, en revanche, vous n’avez aucune idée d’où je viens ni d’où je vais.
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « Même si je suis seul à témoigner en {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} faveur, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} témoignage est vrai. Je sais d’où je suis venu, et je sais où je vais. Mais vous, vous ne savez pas d’où je viens ni où je vais.

sw.L: Yesu akajibu, akawaambia, "Hata kama {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} najishuhudia {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}, ushuhuda {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} ni kweli, kwa sababu najua nilikotoka na ninakokwenda; lakini ninyi hamjui ninakotoka wala ninakokwenda.
sw.B: Yesu akajibu, "Hata nikitoa ushuhuda juu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}, ushuhuda {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} ni kweli, kwa kuwa najua nilikotoka na ninakokwenda. Lakini ninyi hamjui kabisa ninakotoka wala ninakokwenda.
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Hata kama ni {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninayeshuhudia habari {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}, ushuhuda {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} ni kweli. Najua nilikotoka, na najua ninakokwenda. Lakini ninyi hamjui ninakotoka wala ninakokwenda.

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu đáp và nói với họ: "Dù {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} tự làm chứng về mình, lời chứng của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} vẫn là thật, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} biết {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} từ đâu đến và đi đâu; còn các người không biết {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} từ đâu đến hoặc đi đâu.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Dù {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} có tự làm chứng cho mình, lời chứng của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} vẫn là thật, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} biết {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} từ đâu đến và sẽ đi đâu. Còn các người thì chẳng biết {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} từ đâu đến hay sẽ đi đâu.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời: "Dù {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} tự làm chứng về mình, lời chứng của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} vẫn là thật. Ta biết {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} từ đâu đến, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} biết {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đi đâu. Nhưng các người không biết {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} từ đâu đến hay sẽ đi đâu.

ko.L: 예수께서 대답하여 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "내가 나 자신에 대하여 증언하더라도 내 증언은 참되다. 내가 어디에서 왔고 어디로 가는지 알기 때문이다. 그러나 너희는 내가 어디에서 오는지, 또 어디로 가는지 알지 못한다.
ko.B: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "내가 나 자신을 위해 증언한다 하더라도 내 증언은 참되다. 나는 내가 어디에서 왔으며 어디로 가는지 알기 때문이다. 그러나 너희는 내가 어디에서 오는지, 어디로 가는지 전혀 모른다.
ko.R: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "내가 나 자신에 대해 증언하더라도, 내 증언은 참되다. 나는 내가 어디에서 왔는지 안다. 또 내가 어디로 가는지도 안다. 그러나 너희는 내가 어디에서 오는지, 어디로 가는지 모른다.

decisions.choice: true: truthful, a reliable account of the facts
decisions.reason: In 5:31 Jesus said that testimony about himself is "not true", meaning that it does not stand as evidence on its own. Here he makes a different point: whether or not it meets the rule of evidence, what he says about himself is true, because he alone knows the facts, where he came from and where he is going. No other human witness can speak to that. He then grants the legal rule again and meets it by naming the Father as his second witness (8:17-18). The two sayings do not contradict each other: one is about what counts as evidence, the other about whether he speaks the truth.

decisions.choice: where I came from and where I am going: from the Father, and back to the Father
decisions.reason: Jesus has come from God and is returning to the one who sent him (7:28-29, 33; 13:3; 16:28). His opponents think they know where he comes from, Galilee and Nazareth (7:27, 41, 52), and do not understand where he is going (7:35-36); 8:21-22 returns to it.

decisions.choice: I came ... I come: the past tense points to his coming into the world, the present to where he comes from
decisions.reason: In the first half Jesus looks back on the one act of coming from the Father; in the second the present tense speaks of his origin in general, which is what they do not know. "Where I go" is present in form with a future sense: where he is going.

decisions.choice: on my own behalf
decisions.reason: The same words as 5:31 and 8:13, so the legal language stays visible.

decisions.choice: have no idea
decisions.reason: Gives the sharp contrast of the emphatic "you" with Jesus's "I know".

decisions.choice: a mi propio favor
decisions.reason: The same words as 5:31 and 8:13.

decisions.choice: "참되다" for true testimony
decisions.reason: "참되다" covers both truthful and valid as evidence, the two senses at play in 8:13-17; "진리" is kept for the noun "truth".

decisions.choice: "Ta" for himself; "các người" for the Pharisees
decisions.reason: As the guide sets for Jesus speaking to opponents, through the whole passage.

source.text: ὑμεῖς κατὰ τὴν σάρκα κρίνετε, ἐγὼ οὐ κρίνω οὐδένα.

records.literal_gloss: You according to the flesh judge, I not judge no one.

en.L: You judge according to the flesh; I judge no one.
en.B: You judge by human standards; I am not judging anyone.
en.R: You judge people by human standards, only by what you can see. I am not judging anyone.

fr.R: Vous jugez les gens d’une manière humaine, seulement d’après ce que vous voyez. Moi, je ne juge personne.

sw.L: Ninyi mnahukumu kwa kufuata mwili; mimi simhukumu mtu yeyote.
sw.B: Ninyi mnahukumu kwa vipimo vya kibinadamu; mimi simhukumu mtu yeyote.

vi.L: Các người xét đoán theo xác thịt; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không xét đoán ai cả.
vi.B: Các người xét đoán theo tiêu chuẩn loài người; còn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không xét đoán ai cả.
vi.R: Các người xét đoán người khác theo tiêu chuẩn loài người, chỉ theo những gì mắt thấy. Còn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không xét đoán ai cả.

ko.L: 너희는 육체를 따라 판단하지만, 나는 아무도 판단하지 않는다.
ko.B: 너희는 사람의 기준으로 판단하지만, 나는 아무도 판단하지 않는다.
ko.R: 너희는 눈에 보이는 것만 가지고 사람의 기준으로 판단한다. 그러나 나는 아무도 판단하지 않는다.

decisions.choice: according to the flesh: by merely human standards, by outward appearance
alternatives: you judge by my flesh, that is, by my human appearance
decisions.reason: "Flesh" here is human nature in its limits, seeing only the outside. Jesus has already told them not to judge by appearances (7:24); compare 1 Samuel 16:7, where the LORD looks on the heart. Their judgment of him rests on where he seems to come from (7:27, 41-42, 52).

decisions.choice: I judge no one: Jesus does not judge in the way they do, and judging is not the purpose of his coming
decisions.reason: The Father has given all judgment to the Son (5:22, 27), and Jesus will speak of his judgment in the next verse and in 8:26. But he did not come to condemn the world (3:17; 12:47), and he does not pass judgment on mere appearances as they do. The next verse qualifies the statement: when he does judge, his judgment is true.

decisions.choice: you ... I: a sharp contrast
decisions.reason: Both pronouns are written out and set against each other. Greek also allows the double negative, "not ... no one", for a single strong "no one".

decisions.choice: by human standards (B); by human standards, only by what you can see (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (meaning decision m1); Literal keeps "according to the flesh".

decisions.choice: con criterios humanos
decisions.reason: As in English: gives the sense of the idiom (meaning decision m1); Literal keeps "según la carne".

decisions.choice: Vous, vous ... ; {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je ...
alternatives: Vous jugez ... ; je ne juge personne
decisions.reason: French shows the sharp contrast of the two emphatic pronouns (meaning decision m3) with the stressed forms "vous, vous" and "moi, je". The stressed "moi" for Jesus takes the deity_pronoun setting, except at the start of a sentence (R).

source.text: καὶ ἐὰν κρίνω δὲ ἐγώ, ἡ κρίσις ἡ ἐμὴ ἀληθινή ἐστιν, ὅτι μόνος οὐκ εἰμί, ἀλλ’ ἐγὼ καὶ ὁ πέμψας με πατήρ.

records.literal_gloss: And if judge but I, the judgment the mine true is, because alone not I am, but I and the [one] having sent me Father.

en.L: But even if I do judge, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgment is true, because I am not alone, but [it is] I and the Father who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: Yet even if I do judge, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgment is true, because I am not alone in it: it is I together with the Father who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: But even if I do judge, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgment is true. I am not alone when I judge. The Father who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Y aun si yo juzgo, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} juicio es verdadero, porque no estoy solo, sino [que somos] yo y el Padre que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió.

es.R: Pero aun cuando juzgo, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} juicio es verdadero. No estoy solo cuando juzgo. El Padre que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió está conmigo.

fr.L: Et même si je juge, {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} jugement est vrai, parce que je ne suis pas seul, mais [c’est] {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et le Père qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé.
fr.B: Et même si je juge, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} jugement est vrai, parce que je ne suis pas seul à juger : il y a {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et, avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, le Père qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé.
fr.R: Mais même si je juge, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} jugement est vrai. Je ne suis pas seul quand je juge. Le Père qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé est avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.

sw.L: Lakini hata nikihukumu {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, hukumu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ni ya kweli, kwa sababu siko peke {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, bali [ni] mimi na Baba aliyenituma.
sw.B: Lakini hata nikihukumu, hukumu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ni ya kweli, kwa sababu siko peke {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} katika hilo: ni mimi pamoja na Baba aliyenituma.

vi.L: Nhưng nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} có xét đoán, sự xét đoán của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} vẫn là chân thật, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không ở một mình, nhưng [có] {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và Cha, là Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.B: Nhưng dù {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} có xét đoán, sự xét đoán của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} vẫn là đúng thật, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không xét đoán một mình, mà có {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cùng với Cha, Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Nhưng nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} có xét đoán, sự xét đoán của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} vẫn là đúng. Khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} xét đoán, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không ở một mình. Cha, Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, ở với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 그러나 내가 판단하더라도 내 판단은 참되다. 내가 혼자가 아니라, 나와 나를 보내신 아버지께서 [함께하시기] 때문이다.
ko.B: 그러나 내가 판단을 한다 해도 내 판단은 참되다. 나는 혼자 판단하는 것이 아니라, 나를 보내신 아버지와 함께 판단하기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그러나 내가 판단을 하더라도 내 판단은 참되다. 나는 판단할 때 혼자가 아니다. 나를 보내신 아버지께서 나와 함께 계신다.

decisions.choice: the Father who sent me: the SBLGNT reads "Father"
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts lack the word "Father" and read "the one who sent me"; among them are the first hand of Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Bezae. Most manuscripts, including the early papyri, have it, and 8:18 has the same phrase with "Father". The sense is the same either way, since "the one who sent me" always means the Father in John. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: true: genuine, sound, judgment that is what judgment ought to be
decisions.reason: Here John uses a different adjective from the one in 8:13-14 and 8:17. It means real or genuine, as in "the true light" (1:9) and "the true bread" (6:32). Jesus's judgment is the real thing, not a human verdict by appearances (8:15); in 5:30 he called it just, because he seeks the will of the one who sent him.

decisions.choice: even if I do judge: a concession that qualifies 8:15
decisions.reason: The "I" is written out at the end of the clause for weight. Jesus does not take back "I judge no one"; he adds that, when he does judge, he does not judge alone.

decisions.choice: not alone: the Father is with the Son in all he does
decisions.reason: Jesus does nothing on his own (5:19, 30); the one who sent him is with him and has not left him alone (8:29; 16:32). This prepares the two-witness argument of 8:17-18.

decisions.choice: [it is]
decisions.reason: English needs a verb after "but"; the Greek leaves it out.

decisions.choice: in it: it is I together with (B); is with me (R)
alternatives: but I and the Father who sent me (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out what "I and the Father" means here: the Father judges together with him (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: lo hago junto con (B); está conmigo (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: spells out that the Father judges together with him (meaning decision m4).

source.text: καὶ ἐν τῷ νόμῳ δὲ τῷ ὑμετέρῳ γέγραπται ὅτι δύο ἀνθρώπων ἡ μαρτυρία ἀληθής ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: And in the law but the your it has been written that of two people the testimony true is.

en.L: And in your law it is written that the testimony of two {{gender:people|men}} is true.
en.B: Even in your own law it is written that the testimony of two {{gender:people|men}} is true.
en.R: Your own law says that when two {{gender:people|men}} give the same testimony, it counts as true.

es.L: Y en {{plural_you:la ley de ustedes|vuestra ley}} está escrito que el testimonio de dos {{gender:personas|hombres}} es verdadero.
es.B: Incluso en {{plural_you:la propia ley de ustedes|vuestra propia ley}} está escrito que el testimonio de dos {{gender:personas|hombres}} es verdadero.
es.R: {{plural_you:La propia ley de ustedes dice|Vuestra propia ley dice}} que, cuando dos {{gender:personas|hombres}} dan el mismo testimonio, ese testimonio vale como verdadero.

fr.L: Et dans votre Loi, il est écrit que le témoignage de deux {{gender:personnes|hommes}} est vrai.
fr.B: Il est écrit dans votre propre Loi que le témoignage de deux {{gender:personnes|hommes}} est vrai.
fr.R: Votre propre Loi dit que, lorsque deux {{gender:personnes|hommes}} rendent le même témoignage, ce témoignage est reconnu comme vrai.

sw.L: Na katika sheria yenu imeandikwa kwamba ushuhuda wa watu wawili ni kweli.
sw.B: Hata katika sheria yenu wenyewe imeandikwa kwamba ushuhuda wa watu wawili ni kweli.
sw.R: Sheria yenu wenyewe inasema kwamba watu wawili wakitoa ushuhuda ule ule, unahesabiwa kuwa kweli.

vi.L: Và trong luật pháp của các người có chép rằng lời chứng của hai người là thật.
vi.B: Ngay trong luật pháp của các người cũng có chép rằng lời chứng của hai người là thật.
vi.R: Chính luật pháp của các người nói rằng khi hai người cùng làm chứng một điều, thì lời chứng ấy được coi là thật.

ko.L: 너희 율법에도 두 사람의 증언은 참되다고 기록되어 있다.
ko.B: 너희의 율법에도 두 사람의 증언은 참되다고 기록되어 있다.
ko.R: 너희의 율법에도, 두 사람이 같은 증언을 하면 그 증언은 참된 것으로 인정된다고 쓰여 있다.

decisions.choice: the rule of two witnesses in the law of Moses
decisions.reason: The law requires two or three witnesses before a person is convicted (Deuteronomy 17:6; 19:15; compare Numbers 35:30). Jesus gives the sense of the rule, not the words of one verse.

decisions.choice: your law: the law you yourselves hold to and appeal to
alternatives: a law Jesus treats as belonging to them and not to himself
decisions.reason: The possessive is emphatic. Jesus argues from the authority his hearers accept: on their own terms, his testimony stands. He is not setting himself apart from the law of Moses, which he says testifies about him (5:39, 46); he speaks the same way in 10:34, and in 15:25 of "their law". The phrase does mark the distance between Jesus and those who use the law against him.

decisions.choice: two people: two human witnesses; true: valid as evidence
decisions.reason: The word means human beings, without regard to sex. The argument moves from the lesser to the greater: if the word of two human beings stands in court, how much more the testimony of the Son and the Father (8:18). "True" has the legal sense of 8:13.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The witnesses the law speaks of are human beings in general, so the inclusive word is the default and "men" the traditional alternative.

decisions.choice: your own law
decisions.reason: "Own" carries the weight of the emphatic possessive (meaning decision m2). Readable adds "give the same testimony" to make clear that the two witnesses agree.

decisions.choice: {{gender:personas|hombres}}
decisions.reason: Human witnesses in general (meaning decision m3): inclusive default, traditional one tap away.

decisions.choice: la ley de ustedes / vuestra ley
decisions.reason: "Su ley" could be read as "his law"; the span keeps the owner plain, and "propia" carries the emphatic possessive (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: {{gender:personnes|hommes}}
decisions.reason: The witnesses the law speaks of are human beings in general (meaning decision m3), so the inclusive "personnes" is the default and the traditional "hommes" the alternative, as in English.

decisions.choice: watu wawili, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English offers "two men" as the traditional alternative. "Watu" already means people, men or women, so Swahili needs no span here, or in verses 51-52.

decisions.choice: No gender span: "두 사람"
alternatives: a gender setting span as in English
decisions.reason: "사람" means any human being, so Korean has nothing for the gender setting to change.

decisions.choice: "hai người" with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English
decisions.reason: "người" is a person of either sex, so the gender setting has nothing to change.

fr.L: Je suis celui qui rend témoignage de {{deity_pronoun:moi-même|Moi-même}}, et le Père qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé rend témoignage de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. »
fr.B: Je suis un témoin pour {{deity_pronoun:moi-même|Moi-même}}, et le Père qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé rend aussi témoignage de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. »

sw.L: Mimi ndiye ninayejishuhudia {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}, na Baba aliyenituma ananishuhudia."

sw.R: Mimi ni shahidi mmoja, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nashuhudia habari {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}. Baba aliyenituma ndiye shahidi wa pili, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} pia ananishuhudia."

vi.L: Ta là [người] làm chứng về chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và Cha, Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, làm chứng về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."

vi.R: Ta là một nhân chứng, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm chứng về chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Cha, Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, là nhân chứng thứ hai, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cũng làm chứng về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."

ko.L: 나는 나 자신에 대하여 증언하는 사람이고, 나를 보내신 아버지께서도 나에 대하여 증언하신다."

decisions.choice: I am the one who testifies: "I am" with a predicate, ordinary grammar
decisions.reason: The participle is the predicate: Jesus names himself as one of the two witnesses. This is not the absolute "I am" of 8:24, 28 and 58.

decisions.choice: the Father is the second witness
decisions.reason: The two witnesses the law asks for are Jesus and the Father (compare 5:32, 37). The Father testifies through the works he gives the Son to do (5:36; 10:25) and through the Scriptures (5:39). The force of the argument lies in who the second witness is: if they knew the Father, they would accept his testimony (8:19).

decisions.choice: I am one who testifies
alternatives: I am the one who testifies (Literal)
decisions.reason: The point is that Jesus is one of two witnesses; "one who" makes that clear in English without losing the emphatic "I am".

decisions.choice: one witness ... the other witness
decisions.reason: Readable names the two witnesses the law requires (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: un testigo ... el otro testigo
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable names the two witnesses the law requires (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Where is your father?: they take Jesus to mean a human father and ask where this second witness is
alternatives: a question about God, asked in mockery
decisions.reason: A witness had to appear in person. The Pharisees understand Jesus to be speaking of a man and ask him to produce him. The question may also carry a hint about Jesus's birth, as 8:41 may ("We were not born of sexual immorality"), but the text does not say so here.

decisions.choice: they were saying: the Pharisees of 8:13
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject; the Pharisees are the last speakers named. The tense may describe what they kept saying, or simply that they spoke.

decisions.choice: father, lowercase
decisions.reason: The speakers are not thinking of God (meaning decision m1), so "father" is not capitalised in their mouth; in Jesus's answer it is. "Your" takes the setting for pronouns addressed to Jesus.

decisions.choice: the Pharisees
decisions.reason: Readable names the speakers (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: padre, lower case
decisions.reason: The speakers are thinking of a human father (meaning decision m1), so "padre" is not capitalized in their mouth; in Jesus's answer it is.

decisions.choice: "네 아버지" without honorific in the Pharisees' question; "내 아버지", "아버지께서" with it in Jesus's words
decisions.reason: English marks the difference with a lower-case "father"; Korean marks it by speech level. The Pharisees speak of a human father and do not honour him; Jesus speaks of God.

decisions.choice: "cha" lowercase, kept from the start of the question
decisions.reason: They mean a human father, so "cha" is lowercase as in the English; Vietnamese would capitalise it as the first word, so a short "Thế" or "Vậy" ("then") opens the question, bracketed at Literal.

decisions.choice: to know the Son is to know the Father
decisions.reason: Jesus answers that his Father is God, whom they do not know (7:28). The Son makes the Father known (1:18); whoever sees him sees the one who sent him (12:45), and he says the same to his disciples in 14:7-9. Their failure to know Jesus shows that they do not know God.

decisions.choice: if you knew me, you would know: a condition contrary to fact, in the present
alternatives: if you had known me (a past condition)
decisions.reason: The verb "know" has a past form with a present meaning, so the condition speaks about now: they do not know him, and so they do not know the Father.

decisions.choice: my Father, capitalised
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of God, in contrast to the human father the Pharisees had in mind (8:19, first sentence).

decisions.choice: the treasury: the part of the temple courts where the chests for offerings stood
alternatives: a storeroom for the temple's treasure
decisions.reason: Mark 12:41-44 and Luke 21:1-4 tell of people putting money into the treasury, which was a place where anyone could come. Later Jewish tradition (Mishnah Shekalim 6:5) speaks of thirteen collection chests in the temple. The word can also mean a treasure room, but Jesus is teaching in public, so the area by the offering chests is meant, and "in" may mean "at" or "near".

decisions.choice: the temple: the whole temple area with its courts
decisions.reason: This word means the temple courts where people gathered and teachers taught (7:14, 28), not the sanctuary.

decisions.choice: no one seized him because his hour had not yet come
decisions.reason: John says again what he said at 7:30: no one can arrest Jesus before the time the Father has set for his death and glorification (2:4; 12:23; 13:1; 17:1). He was speaking openly in one of the busiest places in the temple, and still no one could take him.

decisions.choice: treasury area, temple courts, arrested (B); near the boxes where people put their offerings, time (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the place (meaning decisions m1 and m2) and use "arrested" as in 7:30 and 7:32. Readable says "time" for the appointed hour, as the book's terms allow and as at 7:30.

decisions.choice: el lugar de las ofrendas (B); cerca de las cajas donde la gente echaba sus ofrendas (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: describes the place (meaning decisions m1, m2). "Hora" at every level, as at 7:30.

decisions.choice: [la salle du] trésor, le temple (L); l’endroit du trésor, la cour du temple (B); près des coffres où les gens mettaient leurs offrandes, la cour du temple (R)
decisions.reason: "Dans le trésor" alone would sound like being inside a hoard. Literal brackets the place word French needs; Balanced and Readable describe the place where the offering chests stood (meaning decision m1). The temple word is the whole temple area (m2), "la cour du temple" at Balanced and Readable, as at 2:14.

decisions.choice: son heure at every level (Readable too)
decisions.reason: As at 2:4 and 7:30: French "son heure n’était pas encore venue" is everyday language for an appointed moment, so Readable keeps the word where English Readable says "time" (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: "헌금함 [곁에서]" (L), "헌금함이 있는 곳" (B); "성전" (L), "성전 뜰" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The treasury was the part of the courts where the offering chests stood, not a vault; "헌금함" names what a reader would see there. The temple is the whole area with its courts, so Balanced and Readable say "성전 뜰".

decisions.choice: "그분의 때" for his hour
decisions.reason: As in 7:30: "때" is the natural Korean for the appointed time and keeps the thread of the "hour" through the book.
